subject: Numeracy
title: Show what we know
subtopics: Revising size, sorting and same and different
objectives: Children will show secure learning of Term 1 ideas through play stations.
Teachers will gather evidence for every child’s Term 1 record.
content: Revising and showing Term 1 learning through play and gathering evidence for the term record.
teachingActivities: Run relaxed play stations; observe and note without testing; offer help only when a child is stuck; celebrate effort.
learnerActivities: Play familiar games, choose stations, show what they know to a friend and tidy up.
resources: A camera or phone for evidence
A small certificate or sticker for each child
assessment: Use the term record to judge each strand: size, same and different, sorting, quantity, counting to three, shape and position. Use two or more occasions before recording Secure.
expectedOutcomes: Completes familiar tasks with confidence at play stations.
Each child has an observation record for Term 1.
crossCurricular: Literacy: songs and rhymes from the term
Social Habits: working with a friend and tidying up

lessons.title: Size, same and different games
lessons.subject: Numeracy
lessons.subtopic: Revising size, sorting and same and different
objectives: Children will revisit big and small, same and different and sorting through games.
successCriteria: Chooses the big or small object on request
Matches an identical pair or sorts a group
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children have met big and small, same and different, sorting, one and lots, counting to three, circles and in, on and under.
resources: Big and small balls, cups and sandals
lessons.starter: Sing "Big, small" and "Same, same, same". Say "Today we play games we know. Show me what you can do!"
teacherActivities: Play "Show me big" and "Show me small" with a mixed basket of objects.
Play "Find my twin" with matching pairs, with children carrying objects to the right place.
Open the colour baskets and ask children to sort objects into groups.
Ask each child to show you one thing they can do well.
learnerActivities: Children choose and show the correct object.
Children find matches and say "same".
Children sort by colour and size.
Child shows a skill and says a word if they can.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Play "Show me big" and "Show me small" with a mixed basket of objects. Children: Children choose and show the correct object.
Step 2. Teacher: Play "Find my twin" with matching pairs, with children carrying objects to the right place. Children: Children find matches and say "same".
Step 3. Teacher: Open the colour baskets and ask children to sort objects into groups. Children: Children sort by colour and size.
Step 4. Teacher: Ask each child to show you one thing they can do well. Children: Child shows a skill and says a word if they can.

practical.title: Revision basket games
steps: Set up three baskets: size, same, sort.
Children visit each basket with a friend.
practical.safety: Use large objects; keep the room tidy and walkways clear.

differentiation.support: Offer one task at a time with an adult partner.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to sort objects in a way of their own and explain it.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: Show me the big one.
questions.expected: Child points to the larger object.

questions.question: Which two are the same?
questions.expected: Child points to a matching pair.

expectedOutcomes: Revisits size, same and different and sorting
lessons.conclusion: Sing "Big, small" and tidy up together.
lessons.homeConnection: Play "big and small" with kitchen items this weekend.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "revisit big and small, same and different and sorting through games" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Counting and one games
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will revisit one, lots, rhymes and counting to three through games.
successCriteria: Counts up to three objects by touching
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children have met big and small, same and different, sorting, one and lots, counting to three, circles and in, on and under.
lessons.starter: Beat the drum three times and say "One, two, three." Say "Let us play the counting games."
teacherActivities: Play "Give me one" and "Give me three" with blocks.
Repeat the rhyme "One, clap! Two, clap! Three, clap!"
Count cups by touching and sliding while the group says the numbers.
Play the goat story and count each goat in.
learnerActivities: Children give one or three blocks.
Children join in with claps.
Children touch and count cups.
Children say the numbers one, two, three.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Play "Give me one" and "Give me three" with blocks. Children: Children give one or three blocks.
Step 2. Teacher: Repeat the rhyme "One, clap! Two, clap! Three, clap!" Children: Children join in with claps.
Step 3. Teacher: Count cups by touching and sliding while the group says the numbers. Children: Children touch and count cups.
Step 4. Teacher: Play the goat story and count each goat in. Children: Children say the numbers one, two, three.

practical.title: Counting stations
steps: Visit stations for blocks, cups and goats.
practical.safety: Use only large objects; supervise at every station.

differentiation.support: Count only to two with the child.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to count four objects with help and say four.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: How many cups?
questions.expected: The correct number up to three.

questions.question: Can you give me one block?

lessons.conclusion: Sing the clapping rhyme and tidy up together.
lessons.homeConnection: Count to three at mealtimes with real objects.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "revisit one, lots, rhymes and counting to three through games" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Shape and position games
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will revisit circles and in, on and under through games.
successCriteria: Follows in, on and under instructions
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children have met big and small, same and different, sorting, one and lots, counting to three, circles and in, on and under.
resources: A box, a cloth and soft toys
lessons.starter: Sing the circle song and "Where is Teddy?" Say "Let us play shape and hide and find games."
teacherActivities: Spread round and not round objects on the mat. Ask "Show me the round one."
Roll a ball and a block and ask "Which rolls?"
Hide Teddy in, on and under and ask "Where is Teddy?"
Play follow the leader through the tunnel, on the bench and under the table.
learnerActivities: Children pick the round objects.
Children point to the ball.
Children find Teddy and say where.
Children follow safely.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Spread round and not round objects on the mat. Ask "Show me the round one." Children: Children pick the round objects.
Step 2. Teacher: Roll a ball and a block and ask "Which rolls?" Children: Children point to the ball.
Step 3. Teacher: Hide Teddy in, on and under and ask "Where is Teddy?" Children: Children find Teddy and say where.
Step 4. Teacher: Play follow the leader through the tunnel, on the bench and under the table. Children: Children follow safely.

practical.title: Shape and position circuit
steps: Set up a round things basket and a position circuit.
Children visit each with a friend.
practical.safety: Supervise the circuit closely; crawling only under tables.

differentiation.support: Offer one task at a time with an adult.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to give a friend a position instruction.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: Show me a circle.
questions.expected: Child points to a round object.

questions.question: Put Teddy under the cloth.
questions.expected: Child places Teddy under the cloth.

expectedOutcomes: Finds circles and follows position instructions
lessons.conclusion: Sing "Where is Teddy?" and say goodbye to Teddy.
lessons.homeConnection: Look for round things and play hide and find at home.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "revisit circles and in, on and under through games" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?

Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Our maths party
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will use Term 1 maths ideas in a pretend party.
successCriteria: Counts or gives one, two or three items
Uses big, small, same or round in play
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children have met big and small, same and different, sorting, one and lots, counting to three, circles and in, on and under.
resources: Plastic cups, plates and toy fruits
A cloth for a party table
lessons.starter: Say "Teddy is having a party! He needs help with the party table." Put out the cloth and the toys.
teacherActivities: Ask children to set the table: "Put one plate for each guest." and "Put one cup on each plate."
Ask them to choose fruit: "Give Teddy three oranges." and "Give the small bear a small cup."
Ask "Where is the cake? In the box! On the table!" and "Which one is round?"
Sing a party song and clap one, two, three.
learnerActivities: Children place one plate and one cup for each guest.
Children count and choose big or small items.
Children use position and shape words.
Children clap and sing together.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Ask children to set the table: "Put one plate for each guest." and "Put one cup on each plate." Children: Children place one plate and one cup for each guest.
Step 2. Teacher: Ask them to choose fruit: "Give Teddy three oranges." and "Give the small bear a small cup." Children: Children count and choose big or small items.
Step 3. Teacher: Ask "Where is the cake? In the box! On the table!" and "Which one is round?" Children: Children use position and shape words.
Step 4. Teacher: Sing a party song and clap one, two, three. Children: Children clap and sing together.

practical.title: Maths party table
steps: Give each child a role such as server or guest.
Children set the table using plates, cups and fruits.
Everyone says what they have done.
practical.safety: Use toy or unbreakable items; keep real food out unless it is a planned snack with allergy checks.

differentiation.support: Give one simple job such as "put one cup on the table".
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to set the table for three guests without help.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: How many cups on the table?
questions.expected: The correct number up to three.

expectedOutcomes: Uses number and shape words in play
Takes a role in a group game
lessons.conclusion: Say thank you to the guests and tidy the party table together.
lessons.homeConnection: Help to lay the table at home: one plate for each person.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "use Term 1 maths ideas in a pretend party" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Show and celebrate
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will show Term 1 learning in familiar games and celebrate their work.
successCriteria: Takes part confidently in at least three familiar tasks
Shows or says one thing they have learned
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children have met big and small, same and different, sorting, one and lots, counting to three, circles and in, on and under.
lessons.starter: Sing a favourite song from the term. Say "Today we show what we know and celebrate."
teacherActivities: Set up six quick stations: size, same, sort, count, circle, position. Spend three minutes at each.
At each station ask a simple question and wait.
Take photographs of each child at work and record levels.
Give each child a sticker or certificate and say one thing they did well.
learnerActivities: Children visit stations in pairs.
Child answers or shows the response.
Children continue playing.
Children receive their award and clap for friends.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Set up six quick stations: size, same, sort, count, circle, position. Spend three minutes at each. Children: Children visit stations in pairs.
Step 2. Teacher: At each station ask a simple question and wait. Children: Child answers or shows the response.
Step 3. Teacher: Take photographs of each child at work and record levels. Children: Children continue playing.
Step 4. Teacher: Give each child a sticker or certificate and say one thing they did well. Children: Children receive their award and clap for friends.

practical.title: Celebration stations
steps: Children visit each with a friend.
Teacher records evidence and takes photos.
practical.safety: Remove small items; supervise all stations; ensure no child feels compared.

differentiation.support: Visit only three stations, with an adult partner at each.
differentiation.extension: Ask a confident child to be a station helper.

assessment.method: Observe each child at the six stations and complete the Term 1 record. Record Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding for each strand: size, same and different, sorting, quantity, counting to three, shape and position.

questions.question: Show me the big one.
questions.expected: Child points to the larger object.

questions.question: How many blocks?
questions.expected: The correct number up to three.

lessons.conclusion: Clap for the whole class and sing the closing song. Send the term note home.
lessons.homeConnection: Parents receive a Term 1 note with one strength, one next step and one home idea.
